identity.description: Pinterest Developer Platform: Pinterest's portal for building apps on the Pinterest API (Conversions, organic Pins and Boards, Ads, Shopping catalogs, analytics).
identity.identity_notes: The developer portal describes the Pinterest product and its API. Pinterest is the vendor; the Pinterest Ads and organic content APIs are all part of this one platform.

auth.oauth_flows: Browser authorization request, redirect to a registered redirect URI, then exchange of the authorization code for an access token (per the getting-started guide). Refresh grant uses the token endpoint, per a search snippet only (not fetched).
auth.token_refresh: Store the access token and refresh it as needed (getting-started guide). Refresh-token rotation and lifetimes are unverified: sources conflict (30-day access token / 1-year refresh in one search snippet, 1-hour access token in a third-party guide).
auth.scopes_notes: Scopes exist and are required per endpoint (per the FAQ summary). Example names such as boards:read, pins:write, ads:read come from a search snippet; the scopes page returned 404 on fetch, so they are unverified. Adding scopes later requires a new token.

access.production_restrictions: Trial access requires Pinterest to approve the app request, which is the most restrictive gate for test credentials. Standard access (needed for public posting) requires a video of the OAuth flow and a live integration, reviewed by Pinterest. Costs are not mentioned on the official access-tiers page; a third-party claim that the API is free is unverified.

write_ops: Create and manage organic Pins and Boards
api.rate_limits: Trial: calls per day per app. Standard: calls per minute, per user, per app. Numeric limits not established from official pages (a third-party 1,000/day figure is unverified).
api.limitations: Trial-created Pins and Boards are visible only to their creator as Sandbox entities. Test tokens expire after 24 hours. Webhooks were not mentioned on any page read; only breaking-change email notifications were found. Access tokens are API-based, not CLI.

open_questions: Auth page (developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/authentication/) and scopes page (developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/scopes/) returned 404; scope names and the Bearer header format need a working source.

Token lifetimes conflict: a search snippet cites a 30-day access token and 1-year refresh token; a third-party guide cites 1 hour; another cites a 60-day refresh token. Needs the official token endpoint reference (developers.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/oauth-token) or a live token response.
Official webhooks: none found on the pages read. Needs a check of the full API reference.
Costs: official pages read do not state pricing. Third-party sources say free; unverified.
Standard review timeline and trial approval timeline are not official; forum reports of 1-2 week waits are anecdotal.

MCP launch status: page says 'Be the first to know when it launches.' Need confirmation that the server is generally available and whether a GitHub repo under the pinterest org exists (a pinterest/mcp-server label was mentioned but no repo link was verified).
Community MCP URLs were from search results only and were not fetched; maintenance status and affiliation are unverified.
Lead not fetched: github.com/pinterest/api-quickstart and github.com/pinterest/pinterest-python-generated-api-client (appear as Pinterest-owned by name; ownership not verified by fetch).
Fetch budget (8) was used up before verifying sandbox token expiry, numeric rate limits, or the full list of endpoints and scopes.
